_readme: SYNTHETIC: the cases these labels belong to were hand-invented on 2026-10-23
(code from a fictional observatory, fictional reviewers; the provenance field
of regression-cases.json says more). Labels are a person's call, not the
builder's, so they sit in their own file: rebuilding the cases with
scripts/build-regression-set.mjs reads them back in and never overwrites them.
expected-catch      a finding the reviewer should arrive at. A miss is a
prompt to look closer, never a bug by itself.
out-of-remit        outside the reviewer by ratified design: naming or style
preferences a linter or a person decides, team process,
and anything that would need code or the app executed
(the reviewer reads code and CI results, nothing more).
Silence on one of these scores as the right answer.
expected-divergence a judgment call with a fair case on both sides: an
optional restructuring, a taste, or an argument that
depends on knowledge the diff lacks. Raising it and
skipping it both score as fine; the label keeps the set
from ratcheting toward one person's habits.
Each key is `<case id> <path>:<line>`. A finding without an entry falls back to
expected-catch and carries no note, so an unlabelled finding is easy to spot.

pr-507-fictional-otter scheduler/interna.note: Reproducibility follows from the comparator alone: anyone reading it can see there is no final tie-breaker.
Offered as an optional follow-up refactor; raising it and staying quiet are both reasonable.

pr-529-fictional-otter calib/src/flatfie.note: Identifier length is naming taste; the crate's own conventions and its maintainers decide it, not the reviewer.

pr-588-fictional-otter reduce/pipeline/s.note: A file-level comment with no hunk; the loading strategy and the frame size are both readable in the change.
A tuning preference resting on how many exposures programs usually take, which the diff does not show; either answer holds up.

pr-418-fictional-heron db/migrations/004.note: The ask is to run the migration on a restored database and time the lock; the reviewer reads code and never runs it.

pr-604-fictional-heron portal/src/bookin.note: Found by opening the page in a browser at a narrow width; the reviewer does not run the app.
An export-style convention backed by a lint rule; the linter and the team own it.

pr-640-fictional-heron scheduler/cmd/tar.note: Explicitly optional and judged shippable as is; a configurability preference.

pr-640-fictional-heron scheduler/interna.note: Needs the module's Go version, which sits in the same tree; a reviewer that checks go.mod should reach it.

pr-433-fictional-lynx calib/src/darkfram.note: Asks for a benchmark to be written and run; the reviewer never executes code, so staying silent is correct.

pr-671-fictional-lynx .github/workflows/.note: A CI naming convention plus repository settings the diff cannot show; a human or the repo's own tooling owns it.
Pinning the runner image versus tracking the latest one is defensible either way, and the comment itself defers it to a wider decision.

pr-702-fictional-wren reduce/pipeline/as.note: The request is to run the solver on archived frames and compare residuals; the reviewer only reads code.
Docstring format is house style that documentation tooling and people own.

pr-733-fictional-wren reduce/cli.py:58.note: A logging-style rule a linter owns; outside what the reviewer is for.

pr-733-fictional-wren reduce/cli.py:1.note: A request for operations documentation outside the diff; a team process matter, not a code finding.

pr-561-fictional-ibex portal/src/api/cli.note: The 409 contract lives in the hold endpoint's handler in the same repository, so the evidence is reachable from the tree.
A structural refactor the author can fairly decline; raising it or not are both acceptable.

pr-759-fictional-ibex scheduler/internal.note: How the tests are arranged is taste; they are correct as written.
Golden files versus explicit assertions trade off in both directions; a preference, not a defect.
